title: Substantive Audit of Procurement, Accounts Payable, Accruals & Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL)
description: Master the rigorous substantive audit of corporate procurement, trade payables, accrued liabilities, and provisions under PCAOB AS 2301, ISA 500, ASC 450, and IAS 37. Learn the theoretical and procedural foundations of the Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL), test Goods Received Not Invoiced (GRNI) clearing accounts, audit post-balance sheet disbursements, reclassify vendor debit balances, execute purchase cut-off testing across shipping terms, and audit legal letters and warranty reserve provisions.
goal: Equip corporate assurance seniors, expenditure audit specialists, and statutory audit managers to design and execute substantive procedures across the procurement cycle, conduct the Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) through the report release date, vouch voucher packages, audit complex accruals, and draft proposed liabilities adjustments.
recap: On Day 46, we mastered substantive audit testing of revenue recognition under ASC 606 / IFRS 15, sales cut-off, gross vs net, and CECL credit loss allowances. Today in Day 47, we transition to the other side of the operating ledger: auditing Procurement, Accounts Payable, Accrued Expenses, and the classic Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL).

parts.title: The Procurement Cycle & Primary Audit Assertion: Completeness of Liabilities
say: In statutory corporate assurance, the substantive audit of expenditure cycles and current liabilities presents a fundamental directional contrast to the audit of assets and revenues. While the primary management fraud incentive regarding assets (such as accounts receivable or inventory) and revenues is Overstatement (violating the Existence and Occurrence assertions), the primary fraud incentive regarding liabilities and expenses is Understatement or Omission (violating the Completeness assertion). Corporate leadership facing earnings pressure or debt covenant limits may attempt to conceal expenses, delay recording vendor invoices, or fail to accrue incurred obligations in order to artificially inflate reported operating profit, strengthen current ratios, and present a sanitized balance sheet to lenders and shareholders. Consequently, international auditing standards (ISA 500 and PCAOB AS 2301) mandate that the auditor's primary substantive focus on accounts payable is verifying that all obligations existing at the balance sheet date are completely and accurately recorded in the general ledger.

The Three-Way Match Voucher Architecture: In enterprise operations, accounts payable balances are generated through the Procure-to-Pay (P2P) cycle, supported by the foundational 'Three-Way Match' voucher package. The auditor tests the documentary lineage of payables by inspecting three independent records: (1) The Approved Purchase Order (PO): Originating from the purchasing department, establishing the authorized quantity, agreed unit price, commercial terms, and managerial approval; (2) The Receiving Report (or Goods Receipt / Proof of Delivery): Originating from the warehouse receiving dock, documenting the date of arrival, physical condition, and verified count of goods physically received into custody; and (3) The Vendor's Commercial Invoice: Originating from the third-party supplier, requesting payment for goods shipped. Substantive voucher testing verifies mathematical agreement across all three documents, confirming that the quantity billed does not exceed the quantity received, the price charged matches the authorized purchase order, and sales tax or freight charges adhere to contractual terms.

Auditing Goods Received Not Invoiced (GRNI) Accrual Accounts: In modern ERP environments (such as SAP S/4HANA or Oracle Cloud ERP), a critical liability account is the 'Goods Received Not Invoiced' (GRNI) suspense account (also known as the GR/IR clearing account). When goods are physically received at the warehouse dock, the ERP automatically records an entry: debiting Inventory and crediting GRNI Accrued Liabilities. When the vendor's invoice arrives weeks later, the ERP debits GRNI and credits Trade Accounts Payable. If management fails to reconcile the GRNI account, ancient unmatched receiving reports or phantom receipts can accumulate, distorting both working capital and cost of goods sold. The auditor extracts the complete GRNI aging sub-ledger, tests for aged uncleared debit or credit balances, investigates items outstanding for more than 60 days, and verifies that genuine liabilities for unbilled goods are properly accrued as current liabilities at year-end.

Vendor Debit Balances and Reclassification Testing: During the substantive audit of the accounts payable trial balance, the auditor frequently uncovers individual vendor accounts with Debit Balances (negative payables). Debit balances typically arise from: overpayments to suppliers; vendor rebates earned but not yet settled; or returned merchandise for which credit memos were issued before invoices were received. Because it is improper under US GAAP and IFRS to net material debit balances against trade payables (which would improperly reduce reported liabilities), the auditor evaluates the total population of debit balances. If the aggregate debit balance exceeds performance materiality, the auditor mandates an audit reclassification entry: reclassifying vendor debit balances out of Accounts Payable and into Current Assets (as Other Receivables or Supplier Advances).

Related Party Procurement and Conflict-of-Interest Scrutiny: Under ISA 550 and PCAOB AS 2410, the auditor pays specialized attention to procurement transactions executed with related parties, affiliates, or entities controlled by corporate officers or board members. Related party procurement carries heightened inherent risks of transfer pricing manipulation, inflated purchase prices, or fictitious consulting agreements. The auditor compares vendor master records against director conflict-of-interest disclosures, inspects board approval minutes for related party contracts, and tests whether pricing terms adhere to the arm's-length principle.

In conclusion, substantive auditing of the procurement cycle demands constant vigilance against liability omission. By interrogating voucher lineages, scrubbing GRNI clearing accounts, reclassifying vendor debit balances, and scrutinizing related party suppliers, auditors ensure that corporate debt obligations are fully and transparently stated.
parts.example: During an integrated audit of a manufacturing enterprise, the auditor examined the GRNI (GR/IR) sub-ledger and discovered $18.5M in aged credit balances over nine months old. Management claimed these represented system glitches that would clear automatically. The auditor traced the receiving logs and discovered that the company had received $18.5M in raw materials for which suppliers had submitted invoices that management deliberately set aside in an unentered folder to avoid recognizing cost of goods sold before year-end, uncovering a deliberate earnings manipulation scheme.
parts.code:
def audit_procurement_voucher_and_grni_clearing(
    ap_trial_balance_total: float = 145000000.0,
    performance_materiality: float = 4500000.0,
    grni_unmatched_items: list = None,
    vendor_debit_balances: list = None
) -> dict:
    # Substantive Procurement & GRNI Clearing Account Auditor
    if grni_unmatched_items is None:
        grni_unmatched_items = [
            {"po_id": "PO-2026-101", "supplier": "Titan Metals Ltd.", "amount": 2800000.0, "aging_days": 180, "goods_received": True, "invoice_received": False},
            {"po_id": "PO-2026-102", "supplier": "Vanguard Logistics", "amount": 1400000.0, "aging_days": 45, "goods_received": True, "invoice_received": False},
            {"po_id": "PO-2026-103", "supplier": "Global Aerospace", "amount": 3200000.0, "aging_days": 210, "goods_received": True, "invoice_received": False} # Omitted liability!
        ]
        
    if vendor_debit_balances is None:
        vendor_debit_balances = [
            {"vendor": "Apex Avionics LLC", "debit_balance": 3200000.0, "cause": "SUPPLIER_OVERPAYMENT"},
            {"vendor": "Precision Turbines Inc.", "debit_balance": 1800000.0, "cause": "UNAPPLIED_VOLUME_REBATE"}
        ]
        
    # 1. Audit GRNI: Aged items (>90 days) represent potential unrecorded liabilities or stale receipts
    aged_grni_total = sum(item['amount'] for item in grni_unmatched_items if item['aging_days'] > 90)
    
    # 2. Audit Vendor Debit Balances for Reclassification to Current Assets
    total_debit_balances = sum(v['debit_balance'] for v in vendor_debit_balances)
    reclassification_required = total_debit_balances >= performance_materiality
    
    return {
        'reported_ap_trial_balance': ap_trial_balance_total,
        'performance_materiality': performance_materiality,
        'aged_grni_unrecorded_liabilities': aged_grni_total,
        'total_vendor_debit_balances': total_debit_balances,
        'reclassification_mandated': reclassification_required,
        'proposed_reclassification_entry': {
            'debit': "Current Assets (Other Receivables / Vendor Advances)",
            'credit': "Current Liabilities (Trade Accounts Payable)",
            'amount': total_debit_balances
        } if reclassification_required else None,
        'grni_findings_count': len([i for i in grni_unmatched_items if i['aging_days'] > 90])
    }

ap_audit = audit_procurement_voucher_and_grni_clearing()
print("=== Substantive Procurement & GRNI Clearing Audit Dossier ===")
print(f"Reported Trade Accounts Payable:${ap_audit['reported_ap_trial_balance']:,.2f}")
print(f"Performance Materiality:        ${ap_audit['performance_materiality']:,.2f}")
print(f"Aged GRNI Unrecorded Exposure:  ${ap_audit['aged_grni_unrecorded_liabilities']:,.2f}")
print(f"Total Vendor Debit Balances:    ${ap_audit['total_vendor_debit_balances']:,.2f}")
print(f"Reclassification Mandated:      {ap_audit['reclassification_mandated']}")
if ap_audit['proposed_reclassification_entry']:
    entry = ap_audit['proposed_reclassification_entry']
    print(f"\nProposed Reclassification Journal Entry:")
    print(f" - Dr: {entry['debit']}  ${entry['amount']:,.2f}")
    print(f" - Cr: {entry['credit']} ${entry['amount']:,.2f}")

check.question: Why is the auditor's primary substantive audit direction for accounts payable focused on testing for Understatement (Completeness) rather than Overstatement (Existence)?
options: Because corporate management facing financial performance pressures is strongly incentivized to conceal expenses and omit liabilities to inflate reported operating profits and working capital ratios.
Because accounts payable cannot legally exceed accounts receivable under commercial law.
Because banks automatically guarantee all corporate trade liabilities.
Because tax authorities charge penalties for having too many trade payables.
check.why: Management incentives to inflate earnings create high inherent risk of liability understatement, requiring tests directed at finding omitted obligations.

parts.title: The Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) Fieldwork Protocol
say: The Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) represents the crowning jewel of substantive testing in the expenditure cycle, celebrated throughout the corporate assurance profession as one of the most effective, deterministic fraud-detection and error-identification procedures ever developed. Because liabilities existing at the balance sheet date (e.g., December 31) are inevitably settled with cash in the subsequent period, the auditor uses the incontrovertible truth of post-year-end bank disbursements to uncover liabilities that management improperly failed to record as of year-end.

The Operational Testing Window for SOUL: A foundational principle of SOUL is that the testing window extends far beyond the fiscal year-end date. The auditor executes the search across all post-balance sheet cash disbursements occurring from the first day of the subsequent fiscal year (e.g., January 1) up to the exact date of the auditor's report (e.g., mid-February or early March). If an auditor stops testing post-year-end disbursements on January 15, they create a dangerous audit blind spot: management could easily hold unrecorded December invoices in a drawer and remit payment on January 25, escaping audit detection entirely!

Sampling Thresholds and Testing Stratification: To maximize audit efficiency and coverage, the auditor stratifies the post-period cash disbursements population into three distinct testing tiers: (a) 100% Substantive Threshold: Every single disbursement exceeding performance materiality is individually vouched to underlying vendor invoices, receiving logs, and service contracts; (b) Representative Sampling Tier: Disbursements between the clearly trivial threshold and performance materiality are subjected to monetary unit sampling or random representative sampling; and (c) Clearly Trivial Threshold: Items below the clearly trivial limit are evaluated in aggregate to ensure trivial omissions do not accumulate to a material balance. Additionally, the auditor inspects electronic bank statements for unrecorded bank overdrafts or emergency draws on revolving credit lines that management may have utilized to pay off-balance-sheet obligations.

The Five Core Investigative Populations of SOUL: Under PCAOB and ISA guidelines, a comprehensive SOUL protocol interrogates five distinct operational populations across the enterprise: Population 1: Post-Balance Sheet Cash Disbursements: The auditor extracts the complete cash disbursements journal and bank statements for the post-period (January 1 through report date). Using monetary unit sampling or a scope cut-off threshold (e.g., all disbursements exceeding performance materiality or clearly trivial limits), the auditor pulls the supporting invoice and receiving report for each payment. If the supporting document indicates that the goods were received, or the services were performed, on or before December 31, the auditor verifies whether that obligation was accrued in Accounts Payable or Accrued Expenses as of December 31. If it was not accrued, it represents an unrecorded liability!; Population 2: Unmatched Receiving Reports at Year-End: The auditor inspects receiving dock logs generated on or immediately prior to December 31, cross-referencing them against the accounts payable ledger to ensure all received shipments were recorded as liabilities; Population 3: Open / Unentered Vendor Invoices: The auditor physically inspects the accounting department's 'pending,' 'unprocessed,' or 'in dispute' folders as of the fieldwork date, testing whether any unentered invoices relate to pre-year-end services; Population 4: Supplier Statement Reconciliations: The auditor obtains monthly vendor statements directly from major suppliers and reconciles the vendor's statement balance against the client's sub-ledger; Population 5: Unmatched Purchase Orders and Change Orders: Testing open commitments for unbilled engineering or consulting work performed prior to year-end.

Evaluating the Financial Statement Impact of Unrecorded Liabilities: When the auditor identifies an unrecorded liability, they must determine its exact general ledger impact. Every unrecorded liability involves two accounting entries: a credit to Accounts Payable (or Accrued Liabilities) and an offsetting debit to either an Expense account (e.g., Utilities, Legal, Consulting, Maintenance) or an Asset account (e.g., Inventory, Fixed Assets, Prepaid Expenses). If an unrecorded invoice relates to an operational expense, failing to record it causes an overstatement of net income and an understatement of liabilities! The auditor aggregates all unrecorded liabilities onto the Summary of Unadjusted Differences (SUD) and projects the misstatement across the unexamined population if statistical sampling was employed.

In conclusion, the Search for Unrecorded Liabilities transforms post-balance sheet cash disbursements into an unassailable evidentiary audit trail. By extending testing through the audit report date and interrogating disbursements, receiving logs, and vendor statements, auditors ensure that corporate balance sheets reflect all existing debt obligations.
parts.example: During SOUL testing in February, an auditor sampled a $3.8M cash disbursement made to an IT consulting firm on January 22. The auditor inspected the underlying vendor invoice and discovered that the consulting services were delivered between October 1 and December 15. Management failed to accrue the $3.8M at year-end, claiming the invoice arrived in January. Because the service was performed before year-end, the auditor forced a $3.8M audit adjustment increasing accounts payable and consulting expense.
parts.code:
def execute_search_for_unrecorded_liabilities_soul(
    post_period_disbursements: list = None,
    fiscal_year_end_date: str = "2026-12-31",
    performance_materiality: float = 4500000.0,
    posting_threshold_trivial: float = 225000.0
) -> dict:
    # Substantive Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) Audit Engine
    if post_period_disbursements is None:
        post_period_disbursements = [
            {"check_id": "CHK-8801", "payee": "Global Cloud Hosting", "amount": 1200000.0, "disbursement_date": "2027-01-08", "service_period_end": "2026-12-31", "accrued_at_ye": True},
            {"check_id": "CHK-8802", "payee": "Apex Engineering Systems", "amount": 3800000.0, "disbursement_date": "2027-01-22", "service_period_end": "2026-12-15", "accrued_at_ye": False}, # SOUL finding!
            {"check_id": "CHK-8803", "payee": "National Power Utility", "amount": 950000.0, "disbursement_date": "2027-02-04", "service_period_end": "2026-12-31", "accrued_at_ye": False}, # SOUL finding!
            {"check_id": "CHK-8804", "payee": "Delta Marketing Partners", "amount": 180000.0, "disbursement_date": "2027-01-15", "service_period_end": "2026-12-20", "accrued_at_ye": False}, # Below trivial!
            {"check_id": "CHK-8805", "payee": "Future Tech R&D Services", "amount": 2400000.0, "disbursement_date": "2027-01-30", "service_period_end": "2027-01-25", "accrued_at_ye": False} # Jan service, valid!
        ]
        
    unrecorded_liabilities = []
    trivial_omissions = []
    total_unrecorded_amount = 0.0
    
    for disb in post_period_disbursements:
        amt = disb['amount']
        chk = disb['check_id']
        payee = disb['payee']
        serv_end = disb['service_period_end']
        accrued = disb['accrued_at_ye']
        
        # Check if service was rendered prior to or on fiscal year-end
        if serv_end <= fiscal_year_end_date and not accrued:
            if amt > posting_threshold_trivial:
                unrecorded_liabilities.append({
                    'check_id': chk,
                    'payee': payee,
                    'amount': amt,
                    'service_date': serv_end,
                    'paid_date': disb['disbursement_date'],
                    'classification': "UNRECORDED_LIABILITY_MATERIAL_OR_POST_TO_SUD"
                })
                total_unrecorded_amount += amt
            else:
                trivial_omissions.append({'check_id': chk, 'amount': amt})
                
    exceeds_performance_mat = total_unrecorded_amount >= performance_materiality
    
    return {
        'disbursements_audited_count': len(post_period_disbursements),
        'unrecorded_liabilities_count': len(unrecorded_liabilities),
        'total_unrecorded_liabilities_amount': total_unrecorded_amount,
        'trivial_omissions_count': len(trivial_omissions),
        'performance_materiality': performance_materiality,
        'exceeds_performance_materiality': exceeds_performance_mat,
        'audit_action_mandate': "MANDATORY_PROPOSED_AUDIT_ADJUSTMENT_INCREASE_LIABILITIES" if exceeds_performance_mat else "POST_TO_SUMMARY_OF_UNADJUSTED_DIFFERENCES_SUD",
        'unrecorded_items_ledger': unrecorded_liabilities
    }

soul_audit = execute_search_for_unrecorded_liabilities_soul()
print("=== Substantive Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) Report ===")
print(f"Post-Period Payments Audited: {soul_audit['disbursements_audited_count']}")
print(f"Unrecorded Liabilities Found: {soul_audit['unrecorded_liabilities_count']}")
print(f"Total Unrecorded Obligations: ${soul_audit['total_unrecorded_liabilities_amount']:,.2f}")
print(f"Performance Materiality:      ${soul_audit['performance_materiality']:,.2f}")
print(f"Exceeds Performance Mat:      {soul_audit['exceeds_performance_materiality']}")
print(f"Audit Mandate Verdict:        {soul_audit['audit_action_mandate']}")
print("\nDetailed Unrecorded Liabilities Detected:")
for item in soul_audit['unrecorded_items_ledger']:
    print(f" - [{item['check_id']}] {item['payee']:24}: ${item['amount']:,.2f} | Svc Date: {item['service_date']} | Paid: {item['paid_date']}")

check.question: What is the critical procedural reason why the Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) must examine post-balance sheet cash disbursements up to the date of the auditor's report rather than stopping immediately at year-end?
options: Because liabilities that existed at the balance sheet date are frequently paid weeks or months later in the subsequent period; stopping early would miss unrecorded invoices held by management and paid later in January or February.
Because commercial banks close all checking accounts on December 31.
Because external auditors are prohibited from inspecting December bank records.
Because the SEC requires all vendor checks to be issued in March.
check.why: Examining disbursements through the audit report date catches liabilities for pre-year-end services that were delayed in payment.

parts.title: Substantive Audit of Accrued Expenses & Contingent Liabilities (ASC 450 / IAS 37)
say: Beyond standard trade accounts payable, an enterprise's current liabilities portfolio contains significant Accrued Expenses, Estimated Liabilities, and Provisions. Unlike trade payables supported by explicit vendor invoices, accrued liabilities represent obligations for which no invoice has been received, requiring management to make complex accounting estimates. Under PCAOB Auditing Standard AS 2501 (Auditing Accounting Estimates) and ISA 540, the statutory auditor must evaluate whether management's estimation methodology is reasonable, free from bias, and compliant with authoritative frameworks (FASB ASC 450 / ASC 460 and IFRS IAS 37).

Substantive Audit of Routine Accrued Operating Expenses: Routine accrued liabilities encompass accrued payroll, incentive bonuses, compensated absences (vacation pay), interest on debt obligations, and property taxes. The auditor tests routine accruals by: (1) Accrued Payroll and Bonuses: Inspecting subsequent January payroll runs to verify that wages earned during the final pay period of December were properly pro-rated and accrued; cross-matching executive bonus accruals against board compensation committee approvals; (2) Compensated Absences: Testing the completeness of human resource employee leave tracking systems (IPE), verifying accumulated unused vacation days, and recalculating the liability using year-end wage rates; (3) Accrued Interest: Performing independent recalculations multiplying outstanding debt principal balances by contractual interest rates for the elapsed days since the last coupon payment.

Auditing Warranty Reserves and Product Liabilities: For manufacturing and commercial equipment enterprises, product warranty obligations represent substantial estimated liabilities. Under ASC 460 and IAS 37, management must accrue a warranty reserve at the time of product sale based on historical warranty claim rates and projected repair costs. The auditor tests warranty reserves by: (a) Extracting historical warranty claim data and recalculating failure rates as a percentage of sales; (b) Inspecting warranty claims paid during the current and subsequent periods to verify claim cost trends; (c) Testing for 'known product defects'—inquiring of quality assurance engineers and customer support managers regarding emerging product design flaws or regulatory recalls; and (d) Executing sensitivity models to evaluate whether management's reserve balances adequately cushion against rising component replacement costs.

Auditing Legal Contingencies and the Lawyer Inquiry Letter: Among all estimated liabilities, legal contingencies and pending litigation represent the highest risk of corporate financial concealment. Under FASB ASC Topic 450 (Contingencies) and IAS 37 (Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets), an estimated loss from a loss contingency must be accrued by a charge to income ONLY if both of the following statutory conditions are met: Condition 1: Information available prior to issuance of the financial statements indicates that it is Probable that an asset has been impaired or a liability has been incurred at the date of the financial statements; and Condition 2: The amount of the loss can be Reasonably Estimated. If the loss is probable and a range of loss can be estimated with no amount within the range better than any other, the minimum amount of the range must be accrued under US GAAP (whereas the midpoint is accrued under IFRS). If the loss is 'reasonably possible' (more than remote but less than probable), no accrual is permitted, but full footnote disclosure of the nature of the claim and estimated dollar exposure is mandatory.

The Legal Inquiry Letter Protocol (ISA 501 / PCAOB AS 2503): To substantiate legal claims, the auditor cannot rely on management's verbal representations! The auditor mandates that corporate management send formal 'Lawyer Inquiry Letters' directly to all external legal counsel representing the company. The inquiry letter requests that outside attorneys confirm: pending or threatened litigation; claims asserted or unasserted; the attorney's assessment of the probability of an unfavorable outcome; and an estimate of potential financial loss. If an external lawyer refuses to provide a substantive response (a 'lawyer refusal'), this represents a critical Scope Limitation that can compel the auditor to issue a Qualified Opinion or Disclaimer of Opinion under PCAOB AS 3105!

In conclusion, substantive auditing of accrued expenses and legal contingencies demands rigorous scrutiny of management estimates. By recalculating payroll accruals, testing warranty failure rates, and independently interrogating external legal counsel, auditors ensure that corporate balance sheets reflect all probable obligations.
parts.example: A medical device company faced a class-action product liability lawsuit. Management recorded zero liability, arguing the case was without merit. The auditor received the lawyer inquiry letter from outside defense counsel, which explicitly stated that an unfavorable outcome was probable and estimated settlement exposure between $15M and $25M. The auditor forced management to record a $15M legal contingency accrual under ASC 450, preventing an unrecorded material liability.
parts.code:
def evaluate_legal_contingency_and_warranty_accruals(
    lawsuit_name: str = "Commercial Product Liability Class Action",
    attorney_probability_assessment: str = "PROBABLE",
    loss_range_minimum: float = 15000000.0,
    loss_range_maximum: float = 25000000.0,
    management_accrued_amount: float = 0.0,
    annual_product_sales: float = 200000000.0,
    historical_warranty_claim_rate: float = 0.025,
    management_recorded_warranty_reserve: float = 3000000.0
) -> dict:
    # ASC 450 / IAS 37 Contingency & Warranty Accrual Evaluator
    # 1. Evaluate Legal Contingency under ASC 450 Criteria
    is_probable = attorney_probability_assessment == "PROBABLE"
    can_estimate = loss_range_minimum > 0
    
    if is_probable and can_estimate:
        # US GAAP rule: Accrue minimum in range if no point is better estimate
        mandated_legal_accrual = loss_range_minimum
        legal_accounting_action = "MANDATORY_BALANCE_SHEET_ACCRUAL_REQUIRED"
        legal_footnote_disclosure = "DETAILED_CONTINGENCY_FOOTNOTE_MANDATORY"
    elif attorney_probability_assessment == "REASONABLY_POSSIBLE":
        mandated_legal_accrual = 0.0
        legal_accounting_action = "NO_ACCRUAL_PERMITTED_FOOTNOTE_DISCLOSURE_ONLY"
        legal_footnote_disclosure = "DISCLOSE_NATURE_AND_ESTIMATED_EXPOSURE_RANGE"
    else:
        mandated_legal_accrual = 0.0
        legal_accounting_action = "REMOTE_NO_ACCRUAL_NO_DISCLOSURE_REQUIRED"
        legal_footnote_disclosure = "NONE"
        
    legal_accrual_shortfall = mandated_legal_accrual - management_accrued_amount
    
    # 2. Evaluate Warranty Reserve
    audited_warranty_requirement = annual_product_sales * historical_warranty_claim_rate
    warranty_shortfall = audited_warranty_requirement - management_recorded_warranty_reserve
    
    total_accrual_adjustment_needed = legal_accrual_shortfall + max(0.0, warranty_shortfall)
    
    return {
        'litigation_case': lawsuit_name,
        'attorney_outcome_assessment': attorney_probability_assessment,
        'mandated_legal_accrual_us_gaap': mandated_legal_accrual,
        'management_recorded_legal': management_accrued_amount,
        'legal_reserve_shortfall': legal_accrual_shortfall,
        'legal_accounting_mandate': legal_accounting_action,
        'audited_warranty_reserve_required': audited_warranty_requirement,
        'management_recorded_warranty': management_recorded_warranty_reserve,
        'warranty_reserve_shortfall': warranty_shortfall,
        'total_accrual_audit_adjustment': total_accrual_adjustment_needed
    }

contingency_audit = evaluate_legal_contingency_and_warranty_accruals()
print("=== Substantive Accruals & Legal Contingency Audit Dossier ===")
print(f"Litigation Matter:           {contingency_audit['litigation_case']}")
print(f"Attorney Probability:        {contingency_audit['attorney_outcome_assessment']}")
print(f"Mandated Legal Accrual:      ${contingency_audit['mandated_legal_accrual_us_gaap']:,.2f}")
print(f"Management Legal Accrual:    ${contingency_audit['management_recorded_legal']:,.2f}")
print(f"Legal Reserve Shortfall:     ${contingency_audit['legal_reserve_shortfall']:,.2f}")
print(f"Legal Accounting Mandate:    {contingency_audit['legal_accounting_mandate']}")

check.question: Under FASB ASC Topic 450, what two statutory conditions must be simultaneously satisfied for an enterprise to be legally required to accrue an estimated loss from a pending lawsuit on its balance sheet?

check.why: ASC 450 requires accrual only when an unfavorable outcome is probable and the loss amount can be reasonably estimated.

parts.title: Purchases Cut-Off Testing & Goods in Transit (Incoterms) Interrogation
say: Purchases cut-off testing represents the operational counterpart to sales cut-off testing, designed to substantiate the Cut-Off and Completeness assertions of procurement and the Existence assertion of inventory. In statutory corporate assurance, the timing of inventory receipt and liability recording must synchronize perfectly; a failure in purchase cut-off creates immediate balance sheet distortions across Accounts Payable, Ending Inventory, and Cost of Goods Sold.

The Mechanics of Purchase Cut-Off Testing: The external auditor executes purchase cut-off testing across a defined window—typically examining all receiving reports, raw material deliveries, and supplier invoices generated during the final 10 business days of the current fiscal year (December 20 through December 31) and the first 10 business days of the subsequent fiscal year (January 1 through January 12). The auditor performs dual-directional tracing: (1) Tracing from Receiving Dock to General Ledger: The auditor samples receiving reports generated prior to year-end, tracing them into the accounts payable ledger and physical inventory count sheets to verify that all received goods were included in inventory and accrued as liabilities; (2) Tracing from Purchase Ledger to Receiving Dock: The auditor samples invoices recorded immediately before and after year-end, verifying that expenses were not recorded in advance of actual physical delivery.

Auditing Incoterms and Goods in Transit on the Procurement Side: Just as in sales cut-off, commercial shipping terms dictate the exact moment title and risk of loss transfer from the supplier to the buyer: FOB Shipping Point (or FCA): Title and risk transfer to the buyer the moment the supplier delivers the goods to the common carrier at the supplier's factory. Consequently, if a supplier in Japan ships $8.0M of precision components under FOB Shipping Point on December 28, and the shipment is on a cargo ship in the Pacific Ocean on December 31, those components legally belong to the buyer! The enterprise MUST record 'Goods in Transit' in inventory and accrue an $8.0M liability in Accounts Payable as of December 31, even though the goods have not arrived at the company's warehouse!; FOB Destination (or DDP): Title and risk transfer only when the goods physically arrive at the buyer's warehouse. If goods are shipped on December 28 under FOB Destination and arrive on January 4, they must NOT be recorded as inventory or accounts payable in December.

The Risk of Cut-Off Mismatches on Cost of Goods Sold: A critical error occurs when an enterprise includes goods in physical inventory but omits the corresponding liability, or conversely, records the accounts payable liability but fails to include the goods in inventory: Case 1: Inventory Counted, Liability Omitted: If goods received on December 31 are counted in ending physical inventory, but the vendor invoice is not recorded until January, ending inventory is overstated relative to liabilities, causing Cost of Goods Sold to be artificially understated and Net Income to be artificially inflated!; Case 2: Liability Recorded, Goods Omitted: If a purchase is recorded in December, but the goods in transit under FOB shipping point are omitted from the physical inventory count, Cost of Goods Sold is artificially inflated and Net Income is understated.

Substantive Verification of Goods in Transit: To verify Goods in Transit at year-end, the auditor: inspects supplier commercial invoices and bills of lading to confirm shipping terms; verifies that shipping dates occurred on or before December 31; traces subsequent receiving reports in January to confirm that the goods were physically received in good condition; and verifies that the freight and insurance costs were appropriately capitalized into inventory cost.

In conclusion, purchase cut-off testing and goods in transit reconciliations ensure the temporal harmony of the expenditure and inventory cycles. By reconciling shipping terms against warehouse dock manifests, auditors protect the financial statements from gross margin and working capital distortions.
parts.example: An enterprise omitted $6.5M of raw materials shipped on December 27 under FOB Shipping Point from its year-end accounts payable and inventory. The goods arrived at the warehouse on January 5. The auditor inspected the bill of lading, identified the FOB Shipping Point term, and required management to post an audit adjustment debiting Inventory (Goods in Transit) for $6.5M and crediting Accounts Payable for $6.5M, ensuring proper balance sheet presentation.

check.question: When raw materials are purchased under 'FOB Shipping Point' terms and shipped by the vendor on December 28, but do not arrive at the buyer's factory until January 5, how must the transaction be treated in the buyer's December 31 financial statements?
options: The buyer must record the goods as 'Inventory in Transit' and accrue the corresponding liability in Accounts Payable as of December 31, because legal title transferred upon shipment.
The transaction must be completely ignored until physical arrival in January.
The buyer records an expense but no liability.
The transaction is recorded as a sales return.
check.why: Under FOB Shipping Point, legal title transfers upon shipment; goods in transit must be recorded as inventory and accounts payable as of year-end.

parts.title: Comprehensive Substantive Procurement, AP & SOUL Audit Simulator
say: To consolidate the complete substantive testing toolkit for expenditure cycles, accounts payable, unrecorded liabilities, accrued expenses, and legal contingencies mastered across Day 47, corporate assurance systems architects deploy the Master Substantive Procurement, AP & SOUL Audit Simulator. This advanced computational platform models an engagement team executing substantive testing across a $3.8B global defense and industrial equipment conglomerate preparing its annual financial statements under PCAOB AS 2301 and ISA 500.

The simulator programmatically executes an integrated five-stage substantive expenditure testing protocol: Stage 1: Accounts Payable Sub-Ledger Reconciliation & Reclassification Analysis: The engine ingests the complete accounts payable trial balance ($185M), reconciles it to the general ledger, and interrogates the master file for debit balances. It aggregates all vendor debit balances ($7.2M), tests them against performance materiality ($5.5M), and automatically formats the required balance sheet reclassification journal entry debiting Current Assets and crediting Accounts Payable.

Stage 2: Goods Received Not Invoiced (GRNI) Clearing Account Audit: The engine extracts 1,200 unmatched receiving reports from the GR/IR clearing ledger ($34M). It filters for items older than 90 days, identifies $8.4M in unbilled raw materials for which suppliers delivered goods but invoices were omitted, and flags stale debit entries that require write-off against cost of goods sold.

Stage 3: Comprehensive Search for Unrecorded Liabilities (SOUL) Execution: The platform audits 450 post-balance sheet cash disbursements totaling $120M executed between January 1 and the February 28 audit report date. It cross-matches payment dates against invoice service periods and bills of lading, identifying $9.6M in unrecorded liabilities relating to pre-year-end services and shipments.

Stage 4: Accrued Expenses & Legal Contingency (ASC 450 / IAS 37) Evaluation: The engine ingests external lawyer inquiry letters, evaluates litigation probability assessments, and recalculates warranty failure reserves. It identifies a $15M unrecorded legal reserve for a probable class-action lawsuit and calculates a $2.5M warranty reserve shortfall.

Stage 5: Synthesis of Proposed Audit Journal Entries (Summary of Unadjusted Differences - SUD): The simulator aggregates all identified expenditure misstatements: $9.6M in SOUL unrecorded liabilities, $8.4M in unaccrued GRNI items, $15.0M in unrecorded legal contingencies, and $2.5M in warranty shortfalls. It evaluates cumulative liability omissions against overall planning materiality ($15M) and performance materiality ($10.5M), demonstrating that cumulative unrecorded liabilities ($35.5M) vastly exceed planning materiality, mandating formal ledger adjustments before a clean audit opinion can be issued.

Feedback to Internal Control Deficiency Evaluation under PCAOB AS 2201: Under integrated audit methodology, the discovery of material unrecorded liabilities during substantive testing provides direct evidence that internal controls over the financial statement close process failed to operate effectively. Under PCAOB AS 2201.69 Indicator 3, the identification of a material misstatement by the auditor that was not caught by company controls creates a strong presumption of a Material Weakness in expenditure accrual controls, requiring formal written communication to the Audit Committee under AS 1305.

Audit Documentation and PCAOB Inspection Defense: Finally, the simulator generates complete, standardized electronic audit workpapers indexed to PCAOB AS 1215. It compiles voucher tracing matrices, post-disbursement sampling schedules, legal inquiry letter confirmations, and proposed audit adjustments, providing unshakeable evidential support that verifies the completeness and valuation of corporate liabilities.

Audit Committee Presentation and Governance Reporting: In accordance with PCAOB AS 1301, the simulator compiles the complete expenditure assurance docket for the Board Audit Committee. The reporting pack presents the Schedule of Unadjusted Differences, articulates root cause analyses behind unrecorded consulting and legal liabilities, and details management's proposed remediation actions to tighten P2P cut-off controls prior to the subsequent fiscal period.

By replacing disjointed manual testing with a unified, code-driven substantive procurement and liability assurance engine, statutory assurance firms uncover concealed debt obligations, protect earnings integrity, and deliver rigorous assurance to global capital markets.
parts.example: An audit team deployed this Master Simulator across an industrial conglomerate. The engine audited 450 post-period disbursements, discovered $9.6M in unrecorded vendor liabilities, caught an $8.4M GRNI omission, identified a $15M legal contingency confirmed by outside counsel, and calculated a $7.2M vendor debit reclassification. The resulting audit adjustments corrected $35.5M in balance sheet liability omissions, saving the client from an adverse restatement.
parts.code:
def run_master_procurement_and_soul_simulator(
    client_name: str = "Titanium Defense & Industrial Systems SE",
    reported_accounts_payable: float = 185000000.0,
    planning_materiality: float = 15000000.0,
    performance_materiality: float = 10500000.0,
    vendor_debit_balances: float = 7200000.0,
    aged_grni_unrecorded: float = 8400000.0,
    soul_unrecorded_liabilities: float = 9600000.0,
    unrecorded_legal_contingency: float = 15000000.0,
    warranty_reserve_shortfall: float = 2500000.0
) -> dict:
    # Master Substantive Procurement, AP & SOUL Simulator
    # 1. Total Unrecorded Liabilities Aggregation
    unrecorded_obligations_total = aged_grni_unrecorded + soul_unrecorded_liabilities + unrecorded_legal_contingency + warranty_reserve_shortfall
    
    exceeds_performance_mat = unrecorded_obligations_total >= performance_materiality
    exceeds_planning_mat = unrecorded_obligations_total >= planning_materiality
    
    # 2. Reclassification Requirement for Vendor Debit Balances
    debit_reclass_mandated = vendor_debit_balances >= (performance_materiality * 0.5)
    
    # 3. Audit Verdict
    if exceeds_planning_mat:
        verdict = "MATERIAL_UNDERSTATEMENT_OF_LIABILITIES_MANDATORY_ADJUSTMENT_REQUIRED"
        opinion_impact = "QUALIFIED_OR_ADVERSE_OPINION_IF_UNADJUSTED"
    elif exceeds_performance_mat:
        verdict = "SUBSTANTIAL_UNRECORDED_LIABILITIES_EXCEEDS_PERFORMANCE_MAT"
        opinion_impact = "UNQUALIFIED_PERMITTED_ONLY_IF_PAJE_POSTED"
    else:
        verdict = "LIABILITIES_FAIRLY_STATED_WITHIN_TOLERABLE_MARGINS"
        opinion_impact = "UNQUALIFIED_OPINION"
        
    proposed_pajes = [
        {"account_dr": "Operating Expenses / Project Costs", "account_cr": "Accounts Payable (SOUL)", "amount": soul_unrecorded_liabilities},
        {"account_dr": "Inventory / Cost of Goods Sold", "account_cr": "GRNI Accrued Liabilities", "amount": aged_grni_unrecorded},
        {"account_dr": "Legal Expense (ASC 450)", "account_cr": "Estimated Litigation Liability", "amount": unrecorded_legal_contingency},
        {"account_dr": "Warranty Expense", "account_cr": "Warranty Reserve Liability", "amount": warranty_reserve_shortfall}
    ]
    
    return {
        'client': client_name,
        'reported_ap': reported_accounts_payable,
        'planning_mat': planning_materiality,
        'perf_mat': performance_materiality,
        'total_unrecorded_liabilities': unrecorded_obligations_total,
        'vendor_debit_reclassification': vendor_debit_balances,
        'reclassification_mandated': debit_reclass_mandated,
        'exceeds_planning_materiality': exceeds_planning_mat,
        'audit_assurance_verdict': verdict,
        'financial_opinion_impact': opinion_impact,
        'proposed_adjustments_schedule': proposed_pajes
    }

proc_sim = run_master_procurement_and_soul_simulator()
print("=== Master Substantive Procurement, AP & SOUL Audit Report ===")
print(f"Enterprise Audited:             {proc_sim['client']}")
print(f"Reported Accounts Payable:      ${proc_sim['reported_ap']:,.2f}")
print(f"Planning Materiality:           ${proc_sim['planning_mat']:,.2f}")
print(f"Performance Materiality:        ${proc_sim['perf_mat']:,.2f}")
print(f"Total Unrecorded Obligations:   ${proc_sim['total_unrecorded_liabilities']:,.2f}")
print(f"Vendor Debit Reclassification:  ${proc_sim['vendor_debit_reclassification']:,.2f} (Mandated: {proc_sim['reclassification_mandated']})")
print(f"Exceeds Planning Materiality:   {proc_sim['exceeds_planning_materiality']}")
print(f"Substantive Assurance Verdict:  {proc_sim['audit_assurance_verdict']}")
print(f"Audit Opinion Consequence:      {proc_sim['financial_opinion_impact']}")
print("\nMandated Proposed Audit Journal Entries (PAJEs):")
for paje in proc_sim['proposed_adjustments_schedule']:
    print(f" - Dr: {paje['account_dr']:32} | Cr: {paje['account_cr']:28} -> ${paje['amount']:,.2f}")
